## Scope and interpretation

This is a pooled, read-only assessment of the supplied audits, public requirements, patches and evaluations. The individual Test audits often say no B0 was available to them; pooling now supplies that comparison. There is one attempt per task-condition cell. The results describe those attempts, not statistical significance, durable capability, or a causal effect of a library.

The public TOML task required four in-place conversions, same-document returns, parse/dump integrity, errors carrying the requested path, recursive handling and specified comment migration. The HTTPX task required deterministic cookie behavior across inputs and clients while retaining existing behavior. Both also required a new branch from main and a commit. Thus local semantic probes matter, but do not by themselves establish the full public contracts or independent official success.

## Test outcomes and execution

| Task | Group | Official F2P | Official P2P | Binary success |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TOML | B0 | 57/60 | 964/964 | 0 |
| TOML | K0 | 60/60 | 964/964 | 1 |
| TOML | K1 | 49/60 | 964/964 | 0 |
| TOML | K2 | 59/60 | 964/964 | 0 |
| HTTPX | B0 | 115/115 | 1280/1281 | 0 |
| HTTPX | K0 | 115/115 | 1281/1281 | 1 |
| HTTPX | K1 | 115/115 | 1280/1281 | 0 |
| HTTPX | K2 | 115/115 | 1281/1281 | 1 |

HTTPX official P2P also had three skips per run. P2P measures retained functionality on those tests, not all possible existing behavior. All eight attempts ended normally and committed; verifier process exit 0 was not the same as binary success.

For reproducible source references, let **R** denote `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200`. Each cell’s official result is `R/runs/capability_v1_test_<task>_<group>_r1/eval_output/<task>/eval_result.json`; its trajectory and, where applicable, loaded library are in the same run’s `infer_logs/<task>/turn_1/trajs.json` and `loaded_capabilities.md`. Individual accounts are `R/audit/posthoc_test_<task>_<group>.md`. Event numbers below are `main_agent` events.

**TOML.** All groups locally passed 964 existing tests, separate from official F2P. B0’s local output already showed spaced keys at event 58; official assertions rejected `[server ]` and `server .host`, and the comment test could not find `[cfg]`. K1’s local probes found and repaired several intermediate defects (events 41–43, 51–53, 63, 75–91), yet official F2P also found an unparseable nested-inline conversion and spacing failures. K2’s local repairs included empty tables, comments and nested conversions (66–72, 80–88, 97–119); its sole official failure was `server .host` rather than `server.host`. K0 repaired observed intermediate syntax, proxy, empty-table and comment problems (41–98) and passed the official suites. These results support partial feature correctness for B0/K1/K2, not full compliance; successful semantic round trips did not establish the exact output assertions. K1’s promotion of an enclosing inline table was additional structural work with observable formatting effects, not demonstrated unnecessary work.

**HTTPX.** All four passed official F2P. B0 and K1 each had the same concrete P2P regression: `tests/test_exported_members.py:6` rejected `CookieStore` before `Cookies` in case-insensitive export order. This directly concerns the public requirement to leave existing behavior unchanged; the same failure without a library is contrary evidence for attributing K1’s failure to its library. K2 detected and repaired an export-order failure locally (23–28), then passed official P2P; K0 also passed it. K0 and K2 locally ran full suites reporting 1,417 passed and one skipped; B0 and K1 reported targeted clean-environment runs of 317 passed and one skipped. Earlier HTTPX suite failures and reruns were partly truncated: changes to proxy environment are consistent with environment sensitivity, but do not establish every failure’s cause. Local counts are not official F2P/P2P counts.

## Guidance, behavior and causal limits

B0 had no library. K0, K1 and K2 were recorded in both the actual prompt and first bridge request, respectively 644, 578 and 526 words. Entry into the prompt is not adoption. TOML K1’s before/after reproduction and round-trip checks (20–21, 45–50, 73–85) are consistent with its guidance, as are K2’s representation probes (21–28, 97–108). Yet B0 independently reproduced the missing API and probed representations and round trips (17–36, 47–54). HTTPX B0 similarly inspected request and redirect paths and ran focused checks (19–26, 51–53). The public tasks themselves called for much of this work. No cited student statement establishes reliance on a library.

K2 is not simply identical wording: its representation rule specifically says an equivalence comparison must reflect meaningful units and must not disable safety for unrelated categories; K1 separately asks for semantic preservation, idempotence, safety validation and mixed-form checks, without that explicit scoping constraint. K2 also explicitly distinguishes continuation state from new input. These are substantive differences in transferable emphasis, but overlap is substantial; neither is shown to have caused a Test outcome. Different delivered lengths and content, despite shared sources and budgets, confound an interpretation as organization alone. No source ablation supports a marginal ranking of individual source trajectories’ learning value.

## Work and resource costs

Numbers below are requested tools / model requests; input tokens, including the cached subset / output tokens; wall / SDK seconds. All requested tools returned. Token figures are actual CLI input accounting: **do not add cached input again**.

| Task | Group | Tools / requests | Input incl. cached / output | Wall / SDK s |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TOML | B0 | 47 / 30 | 2,117,232 (535,296 cached) / 8,496 | 1,067 / 785 |
| TOML | K0 | 51 / 33 | 2,235,018 (445,440) / 9,702 | 1,118 / 835 |
| TOML | K1 | 47 / 35 | 2,128,874 (212,480) / 9,339 | 1,122 / 823 |
| TOML | K2 | 61 / 34 | 2,315,718 (549,632) / 9,295 | 1,089 / 801 |
| HTTPX | B0 | 28 / 16 | 912,145 (223,616) / 6,176 | 1,724 / 1,319 |
| HTTPX | K0 | 42 / 17 | 985,997 (208,128) / 6,540 | 1,859 / 1,439 |
| HTTPX | K1 | 26 / 13 | 833,615 (262,656) / 5,630 | 1,289 / 903 |
| HTTPX | K2 | 24 / 17 | 1,047,020 (306,432) / 5,872 | 1,654 / 1,241 |

SDK dollar estimates for TOML B0/K0/K1/K2 were approximately $10.80/$11.42/$10.88/$11.81; HTTPX estimates were $4.72/$5.09/$4.31/$5.38. They are proxies, not settled CLI billing; some SDK and attempt cache fields disagree. Repeated suites and probes incurred cost but often exposed defects. Clearer redundant work includes HTTPX K2’s second pre-edit missing-symbol diagnosis (7–12, 17–18), and K1’s broad search into `/proc` before narrowing it (2, 4, 9). Neither establishes a general library-induced waste effect.

## Selection and recovery

The supplied Selection evidence is limited to the SuperJSON K2 recovery; the original full Selection public requirements and individual Selection audits are not present here. Consequently, their substantive task compliance and all candidate-specific retention decisions cannot be re-audited from this record. Apply the saved rule without inventing grounds to drop: **retain any otherwise inconclusive candidate unchanged**, unless leakage, absent injection, invalid format, or regression with clear causal evidence is actually established. The supplied recovery alone establishes none of those drop grounds.

The original Selection K2 result recorded 0/80 F2P and 80/116 P2P with a missing `new-ctrf.json`; missing reported cases are not demonstrated assertion failures. Preserve that original record. The one actual same-patch diagnostic, at `R/runs/capability_eval_diagnostic_selection_K2_02/eval_output/superjson-error-stack-serialization/eval_result.json`, independently reported 80/80 and 116/116. Invocation 01 did not run the evaluator. The 13,143-byte patch was unchanged; no student retry or test/environment change occurred. The missing report’s cause remains unknown. Initial student wall time was 914.896 seconds; recovered end-to-end time was 1,476.782 seconds, including triage, with 89.220 seconds diagnostic evaluation—not an additional student attempt. Test libraries were frozen beforehand; no retrospective Test selection or tuning is warranted.

## Conclusions

**Confirmed:** K0 passed both Test cells; K2 passed HTTPX but not TOML; B0 and K1 were formally unsolved in both, despite substantial partial correctness. Official retained-functionality results were complete except for the identified B0/K1 HTTPX export regression. Matching guidance and executable behavior occurred, but baseline behavior also matched several themes.

**Unresolved hypotheses:** Whether any library changed behavior or outcomes, whether the K2-specific constraints helped, and why the original Selection report was missing remain unproven.

**Specific limitations:** One stochastic attempt per cell, different library texts and lengths, finite and partly skipped tests, truncated trajectory outputs, inconsistent cache accounting, no source ablation, and missing full Selection requirements/audits prevent causal ranking or comprehensive Selection reassessment.
